title: FormProvider custom props
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I am trying to migrate a project from V5 to V6, but the the typescript typings limit the way we used react hook forms before. We were able to add custom props to the FormContext (now renamed to FormProvider) and get those with useFormContext. Sadly, I think because of stricter typings, this is not possibly any more.

```
<FormProvider {...methods} fields={fields}></FormProvider>

const { formState, fields } = useFormContext();
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like to know if this was unsupported behaviour in V5 and I should rewrite this usage or if the typings are to strict now.
author: NextNebula

comments.body: Hey @NextNebula thanks for the feature request, I think we have fixed the type on v6 with context, if you need custom props, I would be recommended you build your own context.
Yeah creating our own context instead of mixing it with the form context is probably cleaner code anyway. Thank you!
Thanks for understanding @NextNebula 🙉

satisfaction_conditions: Clarification on whether passing custom props to FormProvider was supported behavior in V5
A recommended alternative approach for handling custom props in V6
Explanation of why the previous approach no longer works in V6

title: How to handle server responses not related to any field?
body:
Hi! 

Is there a proper way to retrieve an error from server (general error, not related to a field) on submission and then show it to users, using the library?

Example: login form with only email and password fields:

form is submitted, but some network error happens on server. I would like to, elegantly, do something like setError("server", "Oh oh! Something went wrong. Please try again later.")

or maybe an "status" object on FormContext, which the user itself could manage. Would this bring performance issues? 

If possible it could be  type safe too. 

with:
useForm<FormValues,FormStatus>()

Just asking, as I don't understand if this implementation would bring unnecessary re-renders, which is one of the biggest pro's of this library. Thanks!
author: outerlook

comments.body:
`setError("server", "serverError", "Oh oh! Something went wrong. Please try again later.")`

it's exactly what you had above. you can invoke that in the `handleSubmit` after your request
I can do that, but wouldn't later typescript complain about me trying to access errors.server, if server isn't a field at all?
you can type that external `serverError` as a field? alternative maybe just use `useState` then.

yes, that would solve it. Feels a little like a workaround, I don't know, but it is simple enough. I know it's hard to say if the library should do something specific for this case, unless it is really really common on other forms. Thanks for your time, @bluebill1049 , that was fast and kind.

no worries :) @outerlook 🙏 We had people suggest to return from handleSubmit and treat them as errors, but it's bit weird at the same time... :( I think keep it simple, it's probably the better solution here.
I agree! Thanks!

What's the best way to reset a network error?
`onSubmit(() => setError('networkError', { message: 'text' })) );`
but then should be something like `onAnyChange` event, where I can reset it. Can't find.

> What's the best way to reset a network error?
> `onSubmit(() => setError('networkError', { message: 'text' })) );`
> but then should be something like `onAnyChange` event, where I can reset it. Can't find.

`clearErrors('networkError')`
@bluebill1049 a method, yes. But when to call it?
yeah, there is no other way. I can't clear it on any input change. For this, I'd need to add `setError('nerworkError', '')` in every change handler.
you can do onChagne as well, just `clearError('xxx')`

title: How to get checkbox checked status not value?
body:
It seems like when using checkboxes it defaults to giving you the `e.target.value` rather than `e.target.checked`. How can I get the checked status rather than the value?

Thanks in advance.
author: Kelbie

comments.body:
Hmmm, I have encountered this issue three times now. 

The difficulty that I am having right now is if you defined a value for checkbox, should you get its `value` or `checked`? if you want only `checked` then what about the user who wants the `value`?

hence I decide to have the following code (in the lib):

`if (isCheckBox(type)) return checked ? value || checked : false;`

if checked you will always get the `value`. for unchecked return `false`. if you only want to know checked or not, you can convert the `value` to boolean.

hope this makes sense, and happy for the good alternative suggestion.

I noticed I was getting either `on` or `false` which I thought was an issue on my end but it sounds like its excepted behavior based on what you said. I want it to return `true` and `false` but the problem is that if you define the value to be true in the html its a string not a boolean which is mildly inconvenient.

Is there a way to specify in the `register` something like:

    register({checkbox: "checked"}) // or 
    register({checkbox: "value"}) 

Then in `react-hook-form` do:

    if (isCheckBox(type)) return e.target[checkbox]
what about do this `!!value` if all you want is true or false

I could but that would require doing that for all my checkboxes in the `onSubmit` callback which doesn't seem like the right place to do it. In the meantime I'll do that but I suggest coming up with some way to specify what you want in the `register`.

i think i have found the solution:

3.21.8-beta.1

please help test above beta version

Just installed it. Seems to be working for me.

I also noticed another potential bug but I'm not sure. Is it expected behavior for nothing to be returned in the `handleSubmit` when using an checkbox input and `ref={register()}`? It only returns the result if you use `register` or `register({})` (with the object)
Thanks for the testing. that's not a bug `ref` takes a callback, going to publish the version and close this issue.
@bluebill1049  onSubmit returns value instead of checked anyway. ... I found it comes when I use validation schema, it changes values from boolean to string
@Zik42 it depends if you have a value attribute in the checkbox.

satisfaction_conditions: A way to get the boolean checked status (true/false) from checkboxes rather than their value
A solution that doesn't require manual conversion of checkbox values in the onSubmit callback
Compatibility with the existing register API pattern
